items.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012
items.q: I want to communicate the close encounter that brings Spielberg back in.

ctx.x: Was there a point where you said I want to be a musician? I want to make a living as a musician.

I was three. I told my mother and she told me this, she said, “Jon you said, ‘I’m going to be a piano player whether you like it or not.’ ‘I’m going to be a piano player the rest of my life whether you like it or not.’” Wow. Because I really wanted it. And in fact she saved, I had a little green 3 X 5 card where I scribbled in pencil, “Someday I will fly all over the globe and play piano.” And she gave me a globe. And I’d spin the globe around and I’d say, “I’m going to play there and I’m going to play piano…

That’s really cool. And I followed a little bit of that path, but I have a feeling that all that, plus with your heavy metal guitar really congealed for you. Because I have this weird thing with guitars. Like guitar players don’t necessarily know what they’re doing. That’s my sense of it. That doesn’t mean they’re not good. I mean I’ve played with some guitar players who if you ask them the chord they’ll show you, “Here’s what it is” and show the hand. Yet their ears are so good I’m jealous.
